title: Admin Users list fixes and exact chat request accept/reject flow (24h resend + permanent 1:1 chat)

requirements.summary: Make /admin/users always show one combined list of all users (approved + unapproved) using the existing admin route/layout/menus.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /admin/users shows a single list/table containing all users (approved, unapproved/pending, rejected, blocked) without requiring any filter toggles to see them.
The screen still uses the existing AdminLayout and AdminRouteGuard flow and does not introduce new routes/screens for user management.
No working admin actions are removed or hidden as a side effect of the list change.

file_operations.description: Switch the data source from pending-only to the full users list (approved + pending + rejected + blocked) while keeping the existing AdminRouteGuard + AdminLayout wrapper and existing actions menu placement.
Extend the existing all-users hook to support admin user management mutations needed by the existing /admin/users screen so it can render all users and keep UI in sync via React Query invalidation.

requirements.summary: Ensure core user details are always visible inline on each /admin/users row (photo, name, email, phone, createdAt).
acceptanceCriteria: Each user row in /admin/users visibly displays: avatar/photo, full name, email, phone number, and a human-readable signup date derived from createdAt.
These fields remain visible when the list is scrolled and regardless of the user status (approved/pending/rejected/blocked).
The existing “View Details” dialog (PendingUserDetailsDialog) may remain, but it is optional and must not be the only place where these core fields are visible.

file_operations.description: Update the existing table columns so every row permanently renders avatar/photo, name, email, phone number, and a formatted joined date/time from users.createdAt for all user statuses; remove any role-based hiding for these fields while preserving the AdminLayout and row Actions column.

requirements.summary: Keep all admin actions working for every user on /admin/users and update the list immediately after each action (no refresh).
acceptanceCriteria: After each admin action is performed, the affected user row updates to reflect the new state (e.g., approved status, blocked state, role) without manual refresh.
Actions remain accessible for the appropriate admin roles (super admin vs helper admin) as currently intended, but core visibility of user details remains unchanged.
If delete is not currently implemented, add it in the same existing actions pattern (dropdown + confirmation) and ensure it removes the user from the list immediately after success.

file_operations.description: Add a 'Delete User' action to the existing dropdown menu pattern (DropdownMenu + AlertDialog confirmation) and keep existing approve/reject/block/promote/view-details actions intact. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Add mutations for approve/reject/block/promote/delete that invalidate the all-users query after success so the list updates immediately without refresh.
Implement Firestore helper capabilities required by /admin/users actions (including deleting a user document) in the same minimal style as existing approve/reject/block/promote helpers.
Wire the extended hook/mutations into the existing AdminUsersScreen so actions operate on any user row and reflect changes immediately via query invalidation (no route changes, no layout changes).

requirements.summary: Enforce exact chat request UI visibility rules on the approved users list (sender only sees 'Request Sent'; receiver sees Accept/Reject only for pending incoming).
acceptanceCriteria: In the ApprovedUsersListView, Accept/Reject controls render only for incoming requests where (toUserId == current user) AND status == pending.
For any sent request, the sender’s UI shows only “Request Sent” (no Accept/Reject, no extra buttons) while it remains pending.
No other request statuses accidentally surface Accept/Reject controls (e.g., accepted/rejected must not show those controls).

file_operations.description: Harden the rendering conditions so Accept/Reject are only shown for pending incoming requests (toUserId === current user) and ensure the sender sees only a 'Request Sent' state for pending outgoing requests; avoid showing any accept/reject controls anywhere else. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: On accept: create/open a permanent private 1:1 chat and show a standard chat UI with history + input; accepted chats remain accessible under Chats.
acceptanceCriteria: Accepting a request transitions the UI into a 1-to-1 chat room view for that pair (either by navigation or in-place, matching the existing routing approach).
The chat room view contains: a message history area and an input box that can send new messages.
After reload/sign-in later, the accepted chat still appears under the user’s Chats (ChatScreen) and reopens correctly.
The solution uses the existing project structure and routing approach (no new project, no major restructure).

file_operations.description: Add/adjust Firestore helper capabilities so accepting a chat request ensures a durable 1:1 chat record exists for the pair and supports loading/sending messages for that chat (persisted across reloads).

After accepting a pending incoming request, transition the user into the existing Chats area (/chat) in a way that opens the relevant 1:1 chat immediately (e.g., via existing navigation + a persisted 'open chat' hint), matching the app’s current manual routing style.

Extend the existing ChatScreen to support opening a selected 1:1 chat and rendering a standard chat UI (message list + input) without introducing a new route; keep the current Chats list view and integrate the room view in-place.

Create a focused chat room UI component used by ChatScreen that renders message history and a send-message input, using existing shadcn-ui primitives already in the project. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: On reject: show a clear rejected state to the sender and enforce a 24-hour resend cooldown based on Firestore timestamps.
acceptanceCriteria: When a request is rejected, the sender’s UI clearly shows a rejected state for that target user (not ambiguous).
Attempting to re-send within 24 hours is blocked (UI disabled and/or backend/client function throws with a clear error message).
After 24 hours have elapsed, the sender can send a new request to the same receiver and then sees only “Request Sent” again.
The 24-hour rule is enforced based on stored timestamps in Firestore (not only in-memory timers) so it persists across reloads/devices.

file_operations.description: Persist a rejection timestamp on chat request rejection and enforce the 24-hour resend rule when sending a new request to the same user by checking stored Firestore timestamps (not in-memory).

Update the per-user request state UI so 'Rejected' is clearly shown to the sender and the resend action is disabled until 24 hours have elapsed, with a clear error/toast message if a resend is attempted too early. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Make all changes immediately verifiable in Draft preview with minimal, scoped UI updates only.
acceptanceCriteria: Draft preview shows updated /admin/users behavior (all users visible + permanent user details).

Draft preview shows updated chat request behaviors (sender-only “Request Sent”, receiver-only Accept/Reject for pending incoming, reject state visibility, 24h resend gating, and accept opens chat UI).
No unrelated UI redesign occurs while making these fixes.

file_operations.description: Ensure the updated 'all users' list/table and permanently visible user fields are displayed directly on /admin/users in Draft (no hidden-only changes), while preserving the existing admin layout and actions menu structure.
Ensure chat request state changes (Request Sent / incoming Accept-Reject / Rejected + cooldown messaging) are visibly reflected in Draft immediately after actions complete.
Ensure the post-accept flow visibly opens a 1:1 chat room UI (messages + input) within the existing /chat screen in Draft so the behavior change is directly confirmable.
